subskills.description: Students blend and read words containing long vowel team patterns by dragging letters into position and confirming the correct spelling. Focus: Recognizing and decoding words with ai, ay, ee, ea, oa, and ow vowel patterns. Examples: rain, play, keep, seat, boat, slow, train, stay, deep, team. Constraints: Provide audio support for sound blends and allow students to manipulate letter tiles to build words in the phonics-blender.
subskills.parent_summary: Reads words with vowel teams like ai, ay, ee, ea, oa, and ow.

subskills.description: Students explore and identify words containing vowel diphthong sounds by sorting patterns into appropriate categories and completing word puzzles. Focus: Identifying and reading words with oi, oy, ou, and ow diphthongs. Examples: coin, toy, out, cow, boil, boy, loud, town, foil, cloud. Constraints: Limit word length to 1-2 syllables and provide clear contrast between different diphthong sounds in the spelling-pattern-explorer.
subskills.parent_summary: Reads words with vowel combinations like oi, oy, ou, and ow.

subskills.description: Students engage with r-controlled vowel words by examining spelling patterns and matching them to their phonetic representations. Focus: Decoding r-controlled vowels (ar, or, er, ir, ur) in common words. Examples: car, fork, her, bird, turn, farm, born, fern, girl, burn. Constraints: Focus on single-syllable word roots to ensure mastery before adding suffixes within the spelling-pattern-explorer.
subskills.parent_summary: Reads words with r-controlled vowels like ar, or, er, ir, and ur.

subskills.description: Students practice reading words that begin or end with consonant digraphs by blending sounds together to form recognizable words. Focus: Decoding words featuring the sh, ch, th, wh, and ph consonant digraphs. Examples: ship, chop, thin, whip, phone, dash, rich, path, moth, graph. Constraints: Isolate the digraph sound at the start of words first, then advance to final position usage in the phonics-blender.
subskills.parent_summary: Reads words with letter pairs like sh, ch, th, wh, and ph.

subskills.description: Students blend sounds into complex words by combining initial and final consonant clusters in various word structures. Focus: Reading words with common initial and final consonant blends like bl, st, mp, and nd. Examples: blue, stop, lamp, sand, blow, star, jump, wind, black, fast. Constraints: Use visual cues to identify the blend segment separately from the vowel-consonant core in the phonics-blender.
subskills.parent_summary: Reads words with consonant blends like bl, st, mp, and nd.

subskills.description: Students listen to words and interact with a visual interface to segment the word into individual syllables. Focus: Developing auditory and visual awareness of syllable counts in words. Examples: apple, tiger, rabbit, basket, tunnel, magnet, button, winter, candle, napkin. Constraints: Provide visual feedback for every correct syllable clap in the syllable-clapper primitive.
subskills.parent_summary: Counts and breaks words into separate syllables, like in rab-bit.

subskills.description: Students build two-syllable words by combining components that follow long-vowel syllable rules. Focus: Decoding two-syllable words where vowels maintain long sounds. Examples: baby, spider, robot, donut, paper, pilot, super, final, local, basic. Constraints: Use a split-screen approach to show the two syllable parts coming together in the word-builder.
subskills.parent_summary: Reads two-syllable words with long vowel sounds, like baby and robot.

subskills.description: Students analyze words with affixes by identifying and attaching common prefixes and suffixes to base words. Focus: Decoding words using knowledge of prefixes (un-, re-, pre-) and suffixes (-ed, -ing, -ly). Examples: unhappy, rewrite, preview, jumped, playing, quickly, redo, dislike, walker, helpful. Constraints: Highlight the base word and affix in different colors in the word-builder.
subskills.parent_summary: Reads words with prefixes like un- and suffixes like -ed or -ing.

subskills.description: Students practice reading high-frequency words that do not follow standard phonetic patterns within a reading passage context. Focus: Recognizing grade-appropriate irregularly spelled words. Examples: said, where, because, through, laugh, friend, would, could, front, light. Constraints: Highlight the irregular word within the text of the decodable-reader and provide instant feedback if misread.
subskills.parent_summary: Reads common words with tricky spellings, like said, where, and through.

subskills.description: Students read short, phonetically controlled passages to demonstrate accurate word recognition. Focus: Building accuracy in reading grade-level decodable text. Examples: 'The cat sat on the mat.', 'Sam had a fast car.', 'The bird can sing.', 'I like to play with my toy.', 'The clouds are big.', 'Help the girl find her book.', 'They will reach the top.', 'The sun is hot today.' Constraints: Measure accuracy and word-reading time automatically within the decodable-reader.
subskills.parent_summary: Reads short grade-level sentences accurately.

subskills.description: Students record themselves reading aloud, practicing appropriate pacing, intonation, and expression. Focus: Enhancing oral reading expression and rate. Examples: Reading a dialogue between characters, reading an enthusiastic informative paragraph, reading a short poem, reading an empathetic narrative, reading a persuasive sentence, reading a list of exclamatory remarks. Constraints: Use audio analysis in the read-aloud-studio to compare against a model reading.
subskills.parent_summary: Reads aloud with good pacing, tone, and expression.

subskills.description: Students identify and correct their own word recognition errors using context clues provided in the sentences they read. Focus: Self-correction and monitoring reading fluency. Examples: 'The boy (ride/rode) his bike to the park.', 'She (read/red) a book about space.', 'The (wind/wine) blew hard.', 'He (lead/led) the way.', 'They (find/found) a gold coin.', 'The (tear/tier) fell from her eye.' Constraints: Provide context-based prompts in the read-aloud-studio for ambiguous or commonly misread words.
subskills.parent_summary: Notices and fixes mistakes while reading using sentence clues.

subskills.description: Express a personal preference about a topic and justify the choice with a simple supporting reason. Focus: State an opinion and provide a logical supporting reason using the OREO model framework. Examples: I like cats, I love pizza, Spring is best, Dogs are great, Books are fun, Parks are nice, Winter is cold, I prefer art. Constraints: Provide a prompt, allow the student to select an opinion, and select a reason from a multiple-choice list to build the sentence.
subskills.parent_summary: Shares an opinion and gives a reason to support it.

subskills.description: Bridge an opinion and a reason by inserting appropriate linking words such as because, also, or another into the sentence structure. Focus: Using transition words to create cohesive relationships between opinions and reasons. Examples: I like dogs because they are playful, Also they are fuzzy, Another reason is they are loyal, I love reading because it is exciting, Also it is educational, Another reason is the stories, I like summer because it is hot, Also I can swim. Constraints: Use drag-and-drop to place linking words into sentence templates.
subskills.parent_summary: Uses connecting words like because, also, and another to link ideas.

subskills.description: Compose a concluding statement that summarizes the opinion expressed in the piece. Focus: Synthesize the opinion into a final wrap-up sentence. Examples: That is why I love dogs, In conclusion cats are the best pets, That is why everyone should read, That is my favorite season, So that is why parks are fun, In short I love art, That is my choice, That is why I like summer. Constraints: Provide a draft paragraph and use multiple-choice to select the best concluding sentence from three options.
subskills.parent_summary: Writes a closing sentence to wrap up an opinion.

subskills.description: Introduce a specific topic using a clear introductory sentence paired with a simple definition. Focus: Defining a subject clearly at the start of an informative text. Examples: A mammal is an animal with fur, Sharks are fish that live in the ocean, The sun is a star that gives us light, An insect is a small bug with six legs, Seeds are what grow into plants, Clouds are made of water vapor, Planets move around the sun, Maps help us find places. Constraints: Use fill-in-the-blanks to complete topic introduction sentences.
subskills.parent_summary: Introduces a topic with a clear starting sentence and simple definition.

subskills.description: Organize related facts into a cohesive paragraph structure containing a topic sentence and supporting details. Focus: Grouping logically connected information to support a central claim. Examples: Sharks hunt for food, They have sharp teeth, They live in deep water, They have gills, They have fins, They are fast swimmers, They breathe underwater, They come in many sizes. Constraints: Use a sorting-station to categorize facts under a given topic sentence before arranging them into a paragraph.
subskills.parent_summary: Groups related facts into a clear paragraph with a main topic sentence.

subskills.description: Draft a concluding statement that effectively brings the informative paragraph to a close. Focus: Creating a summary sentence that reinforces the topic without introducing new facts. Examples: Now you know about sharks, These are facts about insects, That is how seeds grow, This is why the sun is important, So clouds are very helpful, That is how maps work, Now you know all about planets, These are things to know about mammals. Constraints: Provide a body paragraph and offer three concluding options for the student to select the most appropriate one.
subskills.parent_summary: Writes a closing sentence that summarizes an informative paragraph.

subskills.description: Outline a narrative story by identifying the characters, setting, and key events in chronological order. Focus: Structuring the essential components of a story before drafting. Examples: A dog at the park, A girl in the kitchen, A boy at school, A cat in the tree, A bird in the nest, A fish in the bowl, A spider in the web, A mouse in the house. Constraints: Use an interactive storyboard to label story components.
subskills.parent_summary: Plans a story by naming the characters, setting, and main events.

subskills.description: Sequence events in a narrative story using temporal transition words such as first, then, next, and finally. Focus: Establishing a logical time-based flow in storytelling. Examples: First we baked a cake, Then we ate it, Next we cleaned up, Finally we played, First the cat climbed the tree, Then he got stuck, Next the girl helped, Finally he was down. Constraints: Drag temporal transition words into a provided paragraph template.
subskills.parent_summary: Orders story events using words like first, then, next, and finally.

subskills.description: Enhance narrative writing by incorporating descriptive details and writing a meaningful sense of closure. Focus: Adding sensory details and final concluding reflections. Examples: The bright yellow sun shone down, It was a happy day, The dog was very fluffy, The cake smelled delicious, We felt so proud, It was a long day, We were tired, We went home. Constraints: Use a revision-workshop primitive to insert descriptive adjectives and closing statements into pre-written narrative drafts.
subskills.parent_summary: Adds descriptive details and a satisfying ending to a story.

subskills.description: Improve a draft by swapping weak word choices for more descriptive ones and adding necessary details. Focus: Strengthening vocabulary and detail density in writing. Examples: Change 'good' to 'amazing', Change 'went' to 'rushed', Add 'big' to 'dog', Add 'sunny' to 'day', Change 'sad' to 'heartbroken', Change 'fast' to 'swiftly', Add 'colorful' to 'flowers'. Constraints: Use a highlight-and-replace tool in a revision-workshop to identify and update specific words.
subskills.parent_summary: Improves writing by adding details and choosing stronger, more descriptive words.

subskills.description: Combine simple, repetitive sentences and fix run-on sentences to create smoother flow and better sentence variety. Focus: Syntactic manipulation to correct sentence structure and improve readability. Examples: The dog ran. The dog barked. -> The dog ran and barked, I went to the park. It was fun. -> I went to the park and it was fun, He ate the apple. It was sweet. -> He ate the sweet apple. Constraints: Use a sentence-builder tool to combine provided sentences using conjunctions.
subskills.parent_summary: Combines short sentences and fixes run-ons to help writing flow smoothly.

subskills.description: Students listen to short audio passages and select the most important facts to summarize the core events. Focus: Identifying specific key details in informational and narrative text. Examples: The main goal of the scientist, the steps taken by the character, the final outcome of the experiment, the location of the event, the time period described, the reason for the character's choice, the central problem encountered, the solution reached. Constraints: The passage-studio will present a 100-word audio track followed by multiple-choice options to identify the top three key facts, ensuring all answers are directly supported by the text.
subskills.parent_summary: Listens to a passage and picks out the most important facts.

subskills.description: Students analyze a read-aloud passage to extract the main idea or central message through systematic text evidence collection. Focus: Determining the overall point or central message of the narrative or text. Examples: The importance of kindness, the lesson learned by the protagonist, the significance of the invention, the moral of the fable, the primary topic of the report, why the animal adapted to its habitat, how weather affects the local ecosystem, the reason for the city festival. Constraints: The passage-studio must provide a short text segment where the student chooses the one best sentence that summarizes the entire passage from a list of distractors.
subskills.parent_summary: Finds the main idea or central lesson in a story read aloud.

subskills.description: Students engage with passages to answer specific interrogative prompts that probe for deeper comprehension of the speaker's intent and facts. Focus: Demonstrating understanding of who, what, where, when, why, and how questions in relation to the text. Examples: Who was the main character, What happened first, Where did the journey begin, When did the event occur, Why did the character feel sad, How did the problem get solved, What was the setting, Who was involved, Why did the result change, How does the story end. Constraints: The passage-studio will highlight a specific text section and require the student to match or input an answer to a generated interrogative question.
subskills.parent_summary: Answers who, what, where, when, why, and how questions about a story.

subskills.description: Students evaluate short passages to detect information gaps and construct clarifying questions to complete their understanding. Focus: Recognizing missing critical information and formulating questions to obtain it. Examples: The story mentions the character left, but where did they go, The text describes an invention but does not explain its purpose, The passage discusses a plant's growth but misses the environmental need, The speaker describes a storm but fails to mention the location, The report explains a process but skips the final step, The summary omits the name of the main actor, The text ignores the time duration of the experiment, The passage describes a feeling without saying why. Constraints: The passage-studio will prompt the student to identify which question (Who/What/Where/Why) would help them learn more about the missing context.
subskills.parent_summary: Notices missing details in a text and asks questions to learn more.

subskills.description: Students build and refine complete, grammatically correct sentences to convey specific information or ideas clearly. Focus: Construction of full, meaningful sentences in response to given prompts. Examples: The cat sat on the mat, My favorite fruit is a red apple, The sun shines brightly during the day, I went to the park with my friends, The dog barked at the mail carrier, Books provide information about the world, We eat lunch at noon, Science class is very exciting. Constraints: Use the sentence-builder to allow the student to drag-and-drop components or type into the interface, requiring a subject and predicate for every completed sentence.
subskills.parent_summary: Writes complete, grammatically correct sentences to express ideas clearly.

subskills.description: Students perform a digital retelling of a short story while focusing on tone, clarity, and pacing to match the narrative content. Focus: Producing an oral retelling of a story with appropriate expression and volume. Examples: A story about a lost puppy, A short biography of a hero, The process of a butterfly life cycle, A fictional tale of a magic forest, A news report about a local event, The legend of a historic figure, A summary of a community activity, A recount of a personal memory. Constraints: The read-aloud-studio will play a sample, then prompt the student to record their own retelling, providing feedback on fluency and tone clarity.
subskills.parent_summary: Retells a story aloud with clear volume, pacing, and expression.

subskills.description: Categorize nouns to identify collective groups by dragging common items into their correct group containers. Focus: Identifying collective nouns that describe groups of people, animals, or things. Examples: team, bunch, flock, herd, pack, swarm, class, army, school. Constraints: Present the student with a noun and three group labels; student sorts the noun into the matching category.
subskills.parent_summary: Identifies group nouns, such as team, flock, and herd.

subskills.description: Construct sentences by selecting the correct irregular plural noun to complete the statement. Focus: Forming and using irregular plural nouns correctly. Examples: feet, children, mice, teeth, geese, men, women, oxen, lice. Constraints: Use a sentence-builder to present an incomplete sentence and multiple-choice noun forms; student chooses the correct irregular plural form.
subskills.parent_summary: Uses irregular plural words correctly, like feet, children, and mice.

subskills.description: Build sentences that correctly integrate reflexive pronouns to show who performed an action. Focus: Proper usage of reflexive pronouns in standard sentences. Examples: myself, ourselves, themselves, himself, herself, itself, yourselves, yourself. Constraints: Use sentence-builder to allow students to drag the correct reflexive pronoun into an active sentence frame.
subskills.parent_summary: Uses pronouns like myself, himself, and herself correctly in sentences.

subskills.description: Complete sentences by choosing the correct irregular past-tense verb form. Focus: Using irregular past-tense verbs accurately in written context. Examples: sat, hid, told, ran, ate, drank, wrote, spoke, blew. Constraints: Sentence-builder interface displays a sentence with a missing past-tense verb; student selects from a provided list of regular and irregular options.
subskills.parent_summary: Uses past-tense action words with unusual spellings, like ate, ran, and wrote.

subskills.description: Analyze sentences to highlight adjectives and the nouns they modify or adverbs and the verbs they describe. Focus: Identifying the function of adjectives and adverbs. Examples: The big dog, walked quickly, soft bed, jumped high, blue sky, sang loudly, sweet apple, ran fast. Constraints: Use sentence-analyzer to have the student click on a target word then the word it describes.
subskills.parent_summary: Finds describing words that tell about nouns and verbs in sentences.

subskills.description: Build descriptive sentences by selecting appropriate adjectives and adverbs to modify nouns and verbs. Focus: Using adjectives and adverbs in original sentence construction. Examples: The bright sun shines, she walked slowly, he held a heavy bag, they laughed happily, the small cat purred, it rained hard. Constraints: Sentence-builder provides sentence skeleton; student adds modifiers to make the sentence descriptive.
subskills.parent_summary: Writes descriptive sentences using words that describe objects and actions.

subskills.description: Correctly place commas in the greetings and closings of informal letters. Focus: Mastering comma usage for letter conventions. Examples: Dear Sam,, Sincerely,, Hi Maria,, With love,, Dear Grandma,, Best wishes,, Hello class,, Your friend,. Constraints: Sentence-builder shows a letter segment with missing commas; student inserts them at the correct locations.
subskills.parent_summary: Uses commas correctly in letter greetings and closings, like Dear Sam,.

subskills.description: Create contractions by inserting apostrophes into combined word pairs. Focus: Understanding how apostrophes form contractions. Examples: can't, don't, it's, I'm, you're, we've, they're, shouldn't. Constraints: Sentence-builder interface provides word pairs; student identifies the contraction and properly places the apostrophe.
subskills.parent_summary: Places apostrophes correctly to form shortened words like can't and don't.

subskills.description: Form possessive nouns by adding apostrophes to show ownership. Focus: Using apostrophes for singular and plural possessives. Examples: dog's bone, kids' toys, mom's car, trees' leaves, teacher's desk, cats' bowls. Constraints: Sentence-builder provides the phrase; student edits the noun to include the apostrophe in the correct spot.
subskills.parent_summary: Uses apostrophes to show who owns something, like the dog's bone.

subskills.description: Use direct definitions or synonyms provided within a sentence to identify the meaning of unknown words. Focus: Identifying explicit text evidence for word definitions. Examples: The massive, or huge, elephant walked by; A cold breeze made me shiver, or tremble; The chef was diligent, meaning she worked very hard; My dog is obedient, he always listens to me; The tiny, or minuscule, bug crawled away; It was a frigid, or very cold, winter day; The tired runner felt exhausted after the race; The bright, or luminous, star shone at night. Constraints: Provide a clear synonym or definition clause within the sentence; student selects the correct meaning from a multiple-choice list.
subskills.parent_summary: Finds the meaning of new words using clues directly in the sentence.

subskills.description: Infer a word's meaning by examining the surrounding narrative context, setting, or action descriptions. Focus: Using implicit context clues to derive word meaning. Examples: The brave knight entered the dark cave to rescue the queen; The noisy crowd cheered loudly as the team scored a goal; The mysterious map led them to a hidden treasure chest; The gentle wind blew through the trees after the storm; The sudden noise made the cat jump under the sofa; The hungry traveler ate a large meal at the inn; The golden trophy sparkled in the afternoon sun; The wise owl sat in the tree watching the forest. Constraints: Sentences provide contextual scenarios where meaning must be inferred; provide a multiple-choice selection that differentiates between contextually appropriate and incorrect meanings.
subskills.parent_summary: Figures out what unfamiliar words mean using clues from the story.

subskills.description: Determine the meaning of compound words by breaking them down into their individual component parts. Focus: Combining the meaning of two base words to determine the whole. Examples: sunflower, rainstorm, backpack, homework, pancake, toothpaste, campfire, lighthouse. Constraints: Present the compound word and allow the student to select or identify the two base words and their individual meanings to derive the total meaning.
subskills.parent_summary: Figures out compound word meanings by breaking them into smaller words like backpack.

subskills.description: Use common prefixes such as un-, re-, and pre- to modify the meaning of base words. Focus: Applying knowledge of prefixes to change word meaning. Examples: unhappy, undo, redo, rewrite, preheat, prepay, rebuild, unlock. Constraints: Provide a base word and a list of prefixes; student drags the prefix to the base word and selects the correct updated definition.
subskills.parent_summary: Uses prefixes like un-, re-, and pre- to change a word's meaning.

subskills.description: Use common suffixes such as -ful, -less, and -ly to understand how they alter the base word's function. Focus: Applying knowledge of suffixes to determine new word meanings. Examples: helpful, useless, slowly, quickly, careful, fearless, gladly, painful. Constraints: Provide base words and require the student to attach the correct suffix and identify the change in the word's descriptive meaning.
subskills.parent_summary: Uses suffixes like -ful, -less, and -ly to change a word's meaning.

subskills.description: Use a digital glossary or dictionary interface to look up and clarify the meaning of specific vocabulary words. Focus: Navigating alphabetical reference tools to retrieve definitions. Examples: find the meaning of 'enormous', search for 'habitat', locate 'migrate', identify 'calculate', define 'species', look up 'fragile', explore 'orbit', find 'structure'. Constraints: Simulate a dictionary entry display; students must navigate via alphabetical search or scroll to match a word to its provided definition.
subskills.parent_summary: Looks up word definitions using an alphabetical dictionary or glossary.

subskills.description: Connect words to their real-life categories and identify how they are used in everyday contexts. Focus: Sorting words into logical semantic groups. Examples: hammer, wrench, screwdriver (tools); apple, banana, pear (fruits); blue, red, green (colors); shirt, pants, hat (clothes); run, hop, skip (actions); cold, warm, hot (temperatures); cat, dog, bird (pets); piano, guitar, drum (instruments). Constraints: Use a drag-and-drop categorization format where students place words into their correct labeled buckets.
subskills.parent_summary: Sorts words into everyday categories, such as tools, fruits, and colors.

subskills.description: Distinguish subtle shades of meaning among groups of related verbs and adjectives. Focus: Ordering words by intensity or frequency. Examples: drizzle/rain/downpour, warm/hot/scalding, whisper/talk/shout, giggle/laugh/cackle, big/huge/gigantic, fast/speedy/lightning, cold/chilly/freezing, sad/upset/miserable. Constraints: Provide a word sorter primitive where the student arranges the words on a spectrum of intensity or strength.
subskills.parent_summary: Orders related words by strength, such as drizzle, rain, and downpour.

subskills.description: Sequence key events of fables and folktales to identify the beginning, middle, and end of the narrative. Focus: Arranging narrative plot events in chronological order. Examples: introduction of characters, initial conflict, rising action, climax of the challenge, resolution of the problem, final scene, setting description, character actions, plot developments, sequence markers. Constraints: Use the story-map primitive to drag and drop events into the correct chronological buckets; limit stories to short, classic fables.
subskills.parent_summary: Puts the beginning, middle, and end events of a story in order.

subskills.description: Evaluate the narrative to determine the central message or moral of the story. Focus: Inferring the lesson taught by the protagonist's actions or the story's outcome. Examples: Slow and steady wins the race, treat others how you want to be treated, honesty is the best policy, don't be greedy, humility is a virtue, work hard before you play, appearances can be deceiving, kindness is rewarded, courage matters, be prepared. Constraints: Use the story-map primitive to link events to the concluding moral or central lesson.
subskills.parent_summary: Identifies the central message or moral taught by a story.

subskills.description: Analyze how characters react when faced with major challenges or significant story events. Focus: Explaining character response to obstacles. Examples: running away, seeking help, solving the puzzle, speaking up, showing bravery, feeling sad, showing determination, changing strategy, learning a lesson, asking questions. Constraints: Use the character-web primitive to link a specific challenge to a character's internal or external reaction.
subskills.parent_summary: Explains how characters react when facing challenges in a story.

subskills.description: Identify character traits based on specific evidence found in the text. Focus: Supporting character descriptions with textual details. Examples: brave, kind, greedy, curious, helpful, selfish, lazy, adventurous, honest, clever. Constraints: Use the character-web primitive to associate a trait label with text-based evidence snippets or quotes.
subskills.parent_summary: Identifies character traits, such as brave or kind, using evidence from the text.

subskills.description: Recognize and acknowledge the differences between characters' perspectives on the same event. Focus: Comparing how two different characters view a single incident. Examples: the wolf vs. the pigs, the hare vs. the tortoise, a parent vs. a child, a hero vs. a villain, a bystander vs. the participant, a observer vs. the creator, an explorer vs. a local, a newcomer vs. a resident, an older character vs. a younger character, an optimist vs. a pessimist. Constraints: Use the character-web primitive to visually map two conflicting points of view regarding one central narrative event.
subskills.parent_summary: Compares how two different characters view the same event.

subskills.description: Describe the narrative arc by explaining how the beginning introduces the story and the ending concludes the action. Focus: Analyzing the function of story openings and closures. Examples: character introduction, setting the scene, conflict introduction, resolution of the climax, final reflections, character change, loose ends tied up, moral statement, returning to the start, change in setting. Constraints: Use the story-map primitive to label specific parts of the plot diagram as beginning, middle, or end.
subskills.parent_summary: Explains how a story's beginning introduces the action and the ending concludes it.

subskills.description: Classify various texts into literary genres based on their structural and stylistic characteristics. Focus: Distinguishing between genres through content and form. Examples: fable, folktale, realistic fiction, fantasy, poetry, biography, informational text, mystery, historical fiction, myth. Constraints: Use the genre-explorer primitive to sort book titles or short synopses into correct genre categories.
subskills.parent_summary: Sorts stories and texts into genres like fable, fantasy, poetry, and biography.

subskills.description: Identify the overall structure of a narrative using a standard plot diagram. Focus: Mapping out the components of a complete story. Examples: exposition, inciting incident, rising action, climax, falling action, resolution, character goals, central conflict, major events, final outcome. Constraints: Use the story-map primitive to fill in key plot points into a structured diagram layout.
subskills.parent_summary: Identifies key parts of a story's plot, from opening to resolution.

subskills.description: Students read multiple-paragraph informational texts and select the central theme from a provided list of options. Focus: Determining the primary subject matter of a multi-paragraph passage. Examples: A text about honeybees, a text about solar energy, a text about the life of a desert cactus, a text about how mountains form, a text about ocean currents, a text about historical communication, a text about recycling plastics, a text about space exploration. Constraints: The passage studio must present the text on the left and a multiple-choice menu on the right; texts should range from 3-5 paragraphs.
subskills.parent_summary: Identifies the main topic of an informational text with multiple paragraphs.

subskills.description: Students analyze individual paragraphs within a text to identify the specific sub-topic or focus of each section. Focus: Recognizing paragraph-level main ideas within a larger informational text. Examples: A paragraph about how bees make wax, a paragraph about how solar panels capture light, a paragraph about desert animals, a paragraph about types of mountains, a paragraph about ocean depths, a paragraph about the telegraph, a paragraph about the plastic cycle, a paragraph about astronaut training. Constraints: Students drag labels to match each paragraph in the passage studio to its specific topic.
subskills.parent_summary: Finds the main topic of an individual paragraph in an informational text.

subskills.description: Students interact with digital snippets of informational pages to identify how captions, bold terms, and index entries help navigate for information. Focus: Utilizing text features to locate specific details efficiently. Examples: Reading a caption under a diagram, clicking a bold word to reveal a glossary definition, finding a page number for a topic in an index, interpreting a sidebar fact, analyzing a photo label, checking a table of contents, identifying a map key, reading a diagram title. Constraints: Use the text-structure-analyzer to highlight specific features and query their purpose.
subskills.parent_summary: Uses captions, bold words, and indexes to find information in a text.

subskills.description: Students scan informational passages to pinpoint specific facts and pull text-based evidence to answer comprehension questions. Focus: Locating explicit information and evidence to support understanding. Examples: Finding the date an event occurred, naming the materials used in a process, listing the characteristics of an animal, identifying the location of a habitat, finding the scientific name of a plant, identifying the primary fuel source mentioned, stating the steps of a cycle, finding statistics in the text. Constraints: The evidence-finder requires the student to highlight the sentence that supports their answer.
subskills.parent_summary: Finds specific facts in a text to answer reading questions.

subskills.description: Students map the relationship between steps in a process or ideas in a text, explaining how one leads to the next. Focus: Describing connections between events or technical steps. Examples: The sequence of a water cycle, the stages of a butterfly's life, the process of a plant growing from a seed, the steps to building a birdhouse, how rain causes erosion, how inventions changed transportation, the steps of a science experiment, how temperature affects weather patterns. Constraints: The text-structure-analyzer provides a graphical flow chart where the student orders the steps or events correctly.
subskills.parent_summary: Explains how steps in a process or events connect to each other.

subskills.description: Students classify texts by their internal structure, identifying whether the passage is organized as cause-effect, sequence, or comparison. Focus: Recognizing informational text structures. Examples: A weather report (cause-effect), a recipe (sequence), a report comparing two animals (compare-contrast), a history timeline (sequence), an article on pollution (cause-effect), a sports biography (sequence), a comparison of two planets (compare-contrast), a guide to building a shelter (sequence). Constraints: Students use the text-structure-analyzer to drag and drop structural labels onto the appropriate texts.
subskills.parent_summary: Identifies whether a text is organized by sequence, cause-and-effect, or comparison.

subskills.description: Students compare two short texts on the same topic to list what is unique to each and what they share. Focus: Comparing and contrasting two informational texts. Examples: Comparing two texts about the same animal, comparing two texts on different inventions for light, comparing two texts on the weather, comparing two texts about space travel, comparing two texts about historic figures, comparing two texts about plant biology, comparing two texts about ocean habitats, comparing two texts about ancient civilizations. Constraints: Use a Venn diagram interface within the text-structure-analyzer.
subskills.parent_summary: Compares similarities and differences between two texts on the same topic.

subskills.description: Students identify specific statements in two different texts to support their claims about the similarities or differences between them. Focus: Supporting comparisons with direct text evidence. Examples: Identifying a specific sentence in Text A about diet, identifying a specific sentence in Text B about habitat, proving a difference in behavior, proving a similarity in size, validating a claim about the topic, extracting evidence for a classification. Constraints: The evidence-finder allows students to highlight text fragments from both sources to justify their comparison logic.
subskills.parent_summary: Finds evidence in two texts to show how they are similar or different.
